mechanism: STOCHASTIC-SERVER-SIDE-BURST: outliers arrive in tight clusters (2-4 ops within 20-60ms, e.g. r3 i=166/170/175/176 and i=385/386/388; r2 i=4892/4895/4897) with zero client-side gap_before — a sub-60ms BEAM scheduler/reduce-window stall on the substrate queues consecutive requests behind one head-of-line stall on the shared TLS connection. NOT periodic (burst positions 166-4892 across runs, no cadence), NOT client GC (gap_before 0.000-0.031ms), NOT STS re-mint (token pre-minted, 1h TTL, single mint per run), NOT TLS renegotiation (outliers are 5-15ms with 0-connection-count signature; handshake cost is 10-30x larger), NOT host-load correlated (r4 at load 19.0: ZERO outliers, p99 0.943ms, max 2.374ms — better than r1-r3 at load 7.5). T23's 69.7ms outlier did NOT reproduce in 20000 warmed ops (max observed 14.9ms); it is consistent with a connection-pool cold-path event (pooled keep-alive socket replaced mid-run; the first request on the fresh socket pays the full TLS handshake) — unproven here, marked HYPOTHESIS-COLD-PATH.
verdict_standing: NFR-LATENCY cosmos point-read p99 is WITHIN TARGET on warmed serial reads: 0.813-1.04ms across 4 runs x 5000 ops vs 3ms target, including under 19x load. The T23 miss is an outlier-regime event, not the steady-state floor. Standing: PARTIAL_ALIVE (floor re-measured ALIVE <=1.04ms; the 69.7ms cold-path hypothesis unconfirmed — needs instrumented connection-pool telemetry to close).
